however, multiple antibiotic–antibiotic pairs (e.g., aminoglycosides–bacitracin, aminoglycosides–polymyxins, bacitracin–polymyxins) share IDE (insulin-degrading enzyme), a metalloprotease implicated in neuromuscular signaling modulation and acetylcholine receptor regulation.
IDE is a biologically plausible anchor for additive or synergistic neuromuscular blockade, as it cleaves neuropeptides and may influence postsynaptic receptor availability or stability.

No other consistently shared mechanism anchors (e.g., CYPs, ABCB1, KCNH2) appear across the broad antibiotic list — supporting IDE as the only recurrent, functionally relevant node linked to neuromuscular physiology.

text: Other drugs eliminated via renal secretion: Population pharmacokinetic analysis suggests that coadministration of drugs that are secreted by the cationic transport system (e.g., cimetidine, ranitidine, diltiazem, triamterene, verapamil, quinidine, and quinine) decreases the oral clearance of pramipexole by about 20%, while those secreted by the anionic transport system (e.g., cephalosporins, penicillins, indomethacin, hydrochlorothiazide, and chlorpropamide) are likely to have little effect on the oral clearance of pramipexole.
